answer: Split-Key Identity Commitment. Each agent registers one half of a secret; the other half is embedded as a pigment in its published capability manifest. Duplicating an identity requires re-deriving that manifest, and any copy carries a mismatched half unless the attacker replays the original's full history. A central lagoon index records commitment hashes per manifest version, so a resubmitted variant collides and is flagged. Honest agents pay only one store-and-attest step per version; a sybil must forge a coherent vine of manifest revisions matching every prior commitment,
